newsitem.title: USA: Nashville-Davidson Cty, Tenn, trims tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Nashville-Davidson Cty, Tenn, trims tax increase.

text.p: Tennessee's Nashville-Davidson County Metro Council has approved a $1.02 billion budget, cutting back Mayor Phil Bredesen's proposed property tax increase.

Bredesen had proposed raising the tax rate by 73 cents. Before approving the budget Tuesday, the county cut the increase to 54 cents, putting the property tax rate at $4.12 per $100 of assessed value in the Urban Services District and $3.27 per $100 of assessed value in the General Services District.

The new revenues will be divided among school, library and infrastructure projects and fund raises for government workers. The council pared down a propsoed $200 million capital improvements package for schools to $85 million. The plan will eliminate planned renovations but will will provide enough money for added classrooms.
The package still guarantees that the most important components of Bredeson's proposal will be funded, said Shannon Hunt, a spokeswoman for Bredesen.

"Hands down we're one of the lowest taxed cities in the country and this absolutely assures that will continue. In no way does it knock us out of competition in terms of competing with other cities," Hunt said.
